verdict.rationale: YYLO is a CLI orchestrator for coding agents. It can turn GitHub issues into kanban tasks, run them in isolated task worktrees with a delegated subagent such as Claude, and repeat bounded iterations until no open work remains. That plausibly covers an issue-to-fix loop, but the evidence never describes bug diagnosis or fixing as such, and the actual reasoning is delegated to third-party agents. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a bug diagnose-and-fix workflow, any example of an agent reproducing or root-causing a reported bug, and hands-on or independent corroboration of autonomous fixes.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent autonomously diagnose and fix a reported bug

citations.quote: YYLO is a command-line orchestrator for coding agents, repeatable workflows, and receipt-backed repository changes.
Bring Slack messages or GitHub issues into kanban and return completed responses to their source thread.
Repeat bounded YYLO iterations until no open kanban work remains.
yylo init --task "Describe one verifiable outcome" --subagent claude
`task start` freezes the protected target SHA, creates a dedicated branch/worktree, and completes configured dependency hydration before reporting `WORKING`.
